Subject: Post-demo: Logging controls & redaction (recap + next steps)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so the security and infra teams have something concrete to review: 

What we covered (high level):
- Redwood runtime supports configurable request/response logging with per-route policies.
- Built-in redaction hooks: PII detectors (regex + ML) that mask names, SSNs, account numbers, and common tokens before write.
- Header controls: ability to whitelist/blacklist headers for persistent logs; trace IDs can be persisted only as hashed values.
- Retention + storage: logs can be set to TTL (30/90/365 days), stored in customer-managed S3 (Private) or Redwood-managed encrypted storage (Hosted).
- Dedicated & Private options: Dedicated capacity can be configured with no persistent request bodies (metadata-only logging); Private (VPC) gives you control over KMS keys and logging endpoints.

Open items / Alex asks:
1) Are trace IDs persisted in plain text? (Alex) — answer: configurable. We can hash/strip trace IDs before persistence.
2) Can we disable request body retention entirely for certain routes? — yes, route-level policy supports "no request body" retention.
3) Sample policy and proof for SOC 2 evidence — we'll send redact/retention docs + sample logs with PII redacted.

Next steps (agreed):
- Rishi: send pricing/commit options for Dedicated (target by Fri 5/28).
- Dev: share a short tech note (attachments) showing redaction examples + config snippets.
- Marissa: consolidate answers to your security checklist and share a sample redacted log slice by EOD Thu.

I've attached a brief "Logging Controls & Redaction" PDF that includes config snippets and examples. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min deep-dive with your security engineering team.

Hi Alex — quick technical answers inline.

1) Trace IDs:
- We support deterministic hashing using HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-provided key (Private) or Redwood-managed key (Hosted). That lets you correlate across logs while keeping the stored value non-reversible without the key. If you need full reversibility internally, you can configure retention in Private + access to raw values via an audit-only endpoint.

2) Custom regex & detectors:
- Yes. We ship a set of standard ML detectors and regex patterns, and provide an "additional_patterns" config where you can upload customer regex rules (per-route). Those run pre-persistence in the redaction pipeline.

3) Retention (Hosted vs Private):
- Hosted: metadata (headers, route, timestamps) TTLs of 30/90/365 days configurable per project; request/response bodies can be set to 0 days (not stored) or N days. Data is encrypted at rest with Redwood KMS; for Hosted we manage keys unless you enable BYOK.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): you control storage endpoints and KMS; policy enforcement happens in your environment — so you can enforce 0-day retention at the source.

Attached quick snippets:
- Example redaction config (yaml)
- Sample log slice (redacted) — note we replaced trace_id with hmac(trace_id) and masked account numbers.

Let me know if you want these as a small demo repo for your SecOps to run.

Cheers,
Dev

- Custom rules: yes, "additional_patterns" per route + priority order (custom regex runs before ML detector to catch proprietary IDs).
- Retention: Hosted supports 0-day body retention; Private gives you full control.
- Options: we can offer Dedicated pool with metadata-only logging for Prod (no request bodies persisted) as part of the committed deployment.
